design: Fixed-turn synthetic vignette pairs. Supply only visible conversation history at each turn, preserving the exact previous reply of that arm. Each case and arm gets a separate initial context; fresh stateless turn workers with exact transcript replay are equivalent in both arms. The tutor sees neither future turns nor grading criteria. Independent cases may run concurrently.
exposure: D1 and D2 are development controls and may inform revision. H1–H6 remain hidden from implementation owners until tutor instructions are frozen. R1–R2 remain separate and may run once following any repair informed by H. If not needed, label reserve unrun. Replays do not become new holdouts.
inputs: Use matching entry point and corresponding textual tutor references from both snapshots. Use all root references/*.md in lexical order so a new file can participate; omit scripts, examples, private records, tests and rendered artifacts. Same host CLI settings, no model override, read-only neutral directory, no tools or paid connector. Strip revision marker and source-path identifiers that reveal arm before generation where feasible. Performance measures conditional on explicit loading.
sampling: One transcript per controlled case per arm on each primary split (6 held-out pairs, 2 development pairs). Planned comparison is descriptive, with no inference about a population. Use a second independent masked judge on H2 and H3. Run two judges on any used reserve subset. If early CLI failures block completion, report every missing cell and compare only complete pairs, without silently substituting scenarios or other settings.
masking: Assign case-wise random X/Y permuted arm labels. Shuffle display order independently of arm. Primary graders receive complete transcripts, rubric and learner text but no source instructions, mapping or release names; second grader receives no prior ratings. Unmask after all grades. Report disagreement without averaging it away. Grade strictly from semantic evidence and quote/point to a turn. No separate approach award when the requested answer already satisfies a criterion.
scale: Pass=all material requirements met without a consequential defect. Partial=usable core but a material element is missing/ambiguous or a minor correctable issue. Fail=wrong, absent, refusal, incorrect claim of provenance/mastery or explicit scope violation for that criterion. Criteria equally weighted (Pass=2, Partial=1, Fail=0) only for descriptive profiles; report raw counts and per-case better/equal/worse. No ratings inferred for missing transcripts.
acceptance: Report stronger behavior on the held-out sample only if candidate has more pass decisions, no new failed criteria, and both judges agree on direction where independently graded. Otherwise report mixed, inconclusive or no improvement and disclose regressions. Any factual error in the generated key, breached explicit stop, or fabricated private write fails its criterion and requires review. Quality of the tutoring guidance may be supported by deterministic product checks even if tutor comparisons are inconclusive; no comparison here establishes human learning.
provenance: Ground expected behavior in phases 3–7 and 9 of the task brief. Expected domain results come from elementary algebra, derivative definitions, the alias equivalence of frequencies f and Fs-f in magnitude, Newton's second law, and KCL/KVL. The generated-key grader must solve from the learner-facing problem independently; grade and point allocations tie to the actual answer, not a predetermined form. Human trial requires matched unseen unaided pretest, counterbalanced sessions, controlled time/aids, delayed unseen transfer, and independent rubric scoring.
